newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia 1997 inflation seen steady - economists.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia 1997 inflation seen steady - economists.

text.p: Slovenian inflation rose to 8.8 percent in 1996 from 8.6 percent a year ago, but is expected to remain steady in 1997, economists said on Monday.

"Due to expected price rises of electricity and petrol it is hardly possible that inflation will ease below the current level in 1997," Peter Stanovnik, head of the Research Institute at Ljubljana University Economic Faculty, told Reuters.
The government said earlier this year it would start gradual adjustment of energy prices to European Union levels in 1997.

"Currently electricity prices are 20 percent lower that the EU average, while petrol is some 35 percent cheaper. This has to be changed as soon as possible in order to help the energy sector," said Samo Hribar Milic, project manager at the Slovenian Chamber of Economy.

Slovenia is waiting with bated breath for President Milan Kucan to name a candidate for prime minister, following an inconclusive November general election that gave neither left nor right a clear mandate to form a new government.
Milic said the chamber of economy had no general preference for any particular candidate.

He said the new government would have to keep wage growth at least two percentage points below the growth of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997 and significantly reduce public spending in order to keep inflation under control.
"Without that no government will be successful in limiting the inflation rate," Milic said.

The government-sponsored Institute of Macroeconomic Analysis and Development said earlier GDP growth was expected to accelerate to four percent in 1997 from a projected 3.5 percent this year, and inflation was seen steady around nine percent next year.
The government had hoped to reduce inflation to six percent this year but the plan fell by the wayside after it agreed to raise wages in many public sector areas following widespread strikes.
In October the average monthly gross salary in Slovenia was 135,595 tolars ($961), 21.1 percent above the 1995 average. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386 61 1263 644
